findings: The easing adapter retains the selected function and every input across both probes. Known actor identities select the existing indexed helper; no matching identity selects the existing touched helper. Endpoint clocks use the native span-end clamp, output uses the existing pure delta-intersection builder, duplicate indices retain native last-write-wins, and shared script state stays owned by the caller.

The overlay collector performs the AFT-name prepass and exactly two raw global table levels of reference discovery before source probes. Value reachability, registry/global exclusions and explicitly authored registry membership are preserved. Normal Rust default registry identities come from existing owned actor metadata.

The collector traverses highest-index wrappers first, applies native parent-chain rules, skips wrapper children, reads initial state before message probes and the structural Name afterward, preserves live/plain/frame elision policy, reads existing renderer kinds and resolves generic proxy identities after the complete output list is known.

The Rust actor binding stores its default wrapper list in owned metadata. The tree collector now reads that representation when no authored Lua list exists. No wrapper binding, native production implementation, interpreter/C API milestone or manifest was changed.

Cursor observations return the Lua table through the VM stack and immediately pin it until the corresponding native cursor scope ends. Collected output identities hold independent roots while the final batch is built. Only collected output actors are directly retained by the returned batch; temporary traversal alone adds no lasting root. Batch rows reject foreign/released roots and retain owned output data after Lua teardown.

Initial rustfmt caught leading-dot Rust test literals, and the new test used the wrong span enum spelling; both were corrected in the appended fixture portion only. Focused v1 recorded an actual mutable-borrow error in copying/pinning a borrowed VM result; copying the value before pinning fixed it.

Focused v2 passed seven cases and failed four. One exposed missing wrapper metadata fallback in the new collector. Two elision comparisons used native-only prepared_root/top-screen aliases in the new isolated fixture; clearing those fixture aliases aligned both engines. The rename fixture used the semantic native-name method although its assertion required a structural Name edit; it now explicitly edits Name and also exercises semantic-name rewind. Original assertions and the prior 133 tests are preserved.
